name: Oliver Granger
role: Church agent who settled Joseph Smith’s Kirtland debts
dateNote: Section 117 names him at Far West on 8 July 1838, and he died at Kirtland in August 1841.
importance: When Church leaders left Kirtland in 1838, debts and business affairs remained. Section 117 says his name will be held in “sacred remembrance” and tells him to work for the redemption of the First Presidency. It adds that when he falls he will rise again, because his sacrifice matters more than his increase. He returned to Kirtland to settle Joseph Smith’s business and later presided over the Church there.
connections: Husband of Lydia Dibble. Section 117 names him with William Marks and Newel K. Whitney, who were told to leave Kirtland.
reviewNote: Birth (7 February 1794, Phelps, New York), death (23 or 25 August 1841, Kirtland), baptism (about 1832–33), and 1838–39 agency work checked on JSP.
